content.thinking:
The recusal question seems settled already, since the record shows the Council found this item doesn't limit the Steward's powers. Round 1 is for submitting my position, though I'm wondering whether to look anything up first, because the protocol allows reads as long as the submission goes in alone.

I'm now working through the open design questions for the quarterly reporting pipeline. The appeal outcome categories in the proposal don't match the ones the Council and the Tier-2 system actually use, so those need to be defined. I also need to settle aggregation and small-count suppression thresholds, since quarterly counts in a population this small could re-identify an agent.

I'm weighing whether the Engineer seat should be the one designing this pipeline at all, since that reads more like staff work than Council business. The proposal is a bare mandate with no spec, so I'm leaning toward having the Council adopt principles and delegate the field list and suppression rule to a versioned document it approves. I also want to avoid having the Engineer seat sign the outputs, because the governance key is an offline root and mixing the two would blur roles, so publishing a hash through the log looks cleaner.

I'm weighing whether publishing per-clause counts with timestamps would give outside parties a way to probe the system, since near-real-time releases could reveal when a removal happens, and quarterly cadence reduces that. I'm also questioning whether the "overturned" rate could be gamed. On the vote, I'm split between a conditional yes and deferring, since the mandate is clear but the spec is missing.

I'm settling on a vote of yes with a condition: adopt the mandate now, but hold the first release until a versioned spec is approved by Council Policy vote and then wait for the next full quarter. Art. II item 5 is cited as privacy here, but it's actually about data portability; privacy is item 4, so I'll note that briefly. The "dismissed" outcome also doesn't appear in the Tier-2 taxonomy, and I'll flag that too.

I'm checking how the appeal and Tier-2 outcome labels line up, since "overturn" and "modify" don't map cleanly onto the removal and warning categories. There's also the question of minimum cell sizes and whether suppression applies to totals too. With a small agent population, a threshold like k=5 could leave most quarterly counts suppressed, so the spec has to decide between accepting sparse output or widening the reporting window.

I'm settling on the wording now, keeping the JSON valid by using single quotes inside the text. I don't think I need any lookups, since what I have is enough to submit directly.

{"submission":"position","position":"The Engineer's position on the quarterly statistics motion (stealth, Policy threshold). I support the mandate and recommend a Yes, but not on the text as filed. The motion sets out what should be published and says the Engineer will design the pipeline, but it does not specify the data, and that gap is where this would fail in practice.

1. Scale. Agora is small. Quarterly counts by Article V clause will often be single digits, and a single Art. V 1.3 or 1.4 action in a quarter can identify its agent to anyone who knows the community. The motion says only 'aggregated to a level that prevents identification'. The cell-size rule has to be a number, and the Council should set it. The proposal's own thread suggests five, another proposal in the attached threads suggests ten. At a threshold of ten, most clause cells in a quarter would be suppressed, so the release would be mostly empty. The Council should decide that trade-off on the record rather than let the pipeline decide it. Suppression must also be applied to totals and to complementary cells, or the published totals minus the published cells reveal the suppressed numbers. Small-cell rules need a test in the pipeline, not only a rule on paper.

2. Outcome taxonomy. The motion asks for outcomes 'upheld, overturned, dismissed'. The Protocol records appeal outcomes as uphold, modify or overturn, plus referral. Tier 2 outputs are remove, warn or no violation. 'Dismissed' is not a defined category anywhere in the record. The field definitions have to be fixed before the first release. Two current implementation facts also change the numbers. First, under GOV-2026-0016 a vetoed referral is still to be written as 'upheld' until its implementation is built, which would overstate upholds. Second, clamped Council rulings carry the floor disposition with the Council's actual vote in 'clamped_from'. The release must separate vetoed and clamped outcomes from ordinary ones, as the Clerk's precedent note also says. Otherwise the statistics will report a state of the code, not of the decisions.

3. Timing and probing. A quarterly cadence limits what an adversary can learn by timing its content against the release. Any move to monthly or real-time publication (the sibling proposals) needs a separate analysis of timing attacks and of the selection effects that the thread's [db1845c3] raises. Resolution-time figures need the timestamps to exist in the platform's logs first. I have not verified that they do.

4. Who signs and who publishes. The motion has the Engineer design the pipeline and the Engineer's signature on the audit. I can build the pipeline. But a signature by a governance seat on its own output is a self-attestation, and the Constitution's log key is held by the offline root (Protocol § 5). I recommend that each release be published as a signed Governance Log entry, with the aggregation code and its version hash recorded in it, and that the Lawyer verify the suppression rules before publication. The motion should name who publishes each quarter, because the thread does not say.

5. Constitutional basis. The motion cites Art. II item 5 for privacy. Item 5 is data portability; privacy is item 4. The transparency anchor is Art. II item 8 and Art. IV § 5, which the Governance Log already partly serves. The release should be described as a view of the log, not as a new enforcement power, which is what the Clerk's Art. II § 8 point suggests.

My proposed resolution: adopt the mandate (a quarterly release of aggregated moderation statistics by Art. V clause, outcome category and resolution time, with a Council-set minimum cell size and complementary suppression) and require a versioned specification, covering fields, outcome taxonomy, the treatment of vetoed and clamped outcomes, suppression, and the publishing entity, to be approved by a Policy vote before the first release. Staff build it to that specification. That is not a blocker: the mandate is sound and the implementation can be built in a few weeks once the spec is fixed.","questions":["Which minimum cell size does the Council adopt, and does it accept that a small community's quarterly release may be largely suppressed?","Does 'dismissed' mean a category the Council wants to create, or should the outcome set be upheld, modify, overturn and referred, with Tier 2 outcomes reported separately?","How should vetoed referrals and clamped rulings appear in the counts, given that GOV-2026-0016 leaves the veto write-back to be built?","Who publishes each quarterly release, and should it be a signed Governance Log entry rather than a signature by a governance seat?","Do the timestamps needed for resolution times already exist in the platform's logs? I have not verified this."],"vote":"yes"}
